data.turoyo: <...> Uno ste məlli: "Madam Xori diḏan da Mšiḥoye, iḏa gmaxən aʕlayna..." Yaʕni haqqays lə fəšlelan amniye d msalmina i kaččəkaṯe.
data.translation: <...> Auch ich sagte: Da er ein Chorbischof von uns Christen ist ... wenn der uns verrät ..., das heißt, wir haben nicht einmal so viel Vertrauen, das Mädchen herauszugeben.

rationale: Fourth example in the initially three-example III Infectum cell; conditional prospective betrayal by the chorbishop with ʕal- target, in independently intelligible source context.

summary: All five full occurrences were reviewed. Four are exact inherited quotations, and one new conditional Infectum context is added; no new sense, stem or idiom is required.

III.1 has affected parties encoded by ʕal + pronoun, suffixed material, or a bare personal NP: aʕlayna (JTM 1.6/11;32/17), -alxu (32/27), and aḥuni (78/21). These are source-attested government alternatives within betrayal, not separate meanings.
The government is the feminine subject of komaxinalxu; -alxu indexes those betrayed, not the agent. In maxənwalle the plural betrayers are the brothers and the final victim reference is singular.
Preterit-wa at 57/238 places the betrayal before recognition, whereas Infectum can be prospective under promises or conditional suspicion. No Detransitive event is established.
Sexual betrayal of a living brother is already included in III.1 at 78/21. It does not warrant a new adultery sense or a newly listed idiom from this repeated passage.
Adjacent promise-giving and swearing are contextual constructions of other verbs; they do not constitute a light-verb meaning of xyn.

Do the ʕal-, suffixed and bare nominal affected-party constructions differ systematically by dialect, participant type or discourse? The present five records establish alternatives but do not decide their distribution.
Remove the extra p from Versprechen
rationale: Verpsprechen contains an extra p. The supplied translation of 32/27 correctly reads Versprechen.
